meta.title: MRI breast pipeline: Oncotype DX risk from MRI + tabular data
meta.oneLiner: Predicts whether a breast cancer patient's Oncotype DX recurrence score is high (>18) or low (<=18) from DCE-MRI images and tabular features, using patient-grouped nested cross-validation and late fusion of an image model and a tabular model.
meta.howToRead: Read the columns from left to right. Data preparation (optional) produces input files. The controller turns a config file into one command per experiment. Train fits one image model and one tabular model per cross-validation fold. Validate scores the held-out patients, fuses the two models and tunes decision thresholds. Summarize ranks all configurations.

entryPoints.role: Bash controller (Slurm arrays, or --local on this machine)
Python composition root; the only place that builds concrete sources, mask providers and branch trainers
Separate data-preparation tools with their own optional dependencies (.[prepare], .[segment])
Bash-readable configuration: PATHS, TRAIN, TRAIN_GRID, VALIDATE, VALIDATE_GRID, SUMMARIZE
30-run screening campaign: shared baseline + one-factor variations; submits MRI-CORE prerequisites, train -> validate per run, one summary
Single field registry read by both Bash and Python (key, section, type, default, choices, identity)

meta.labelNote: Label: Oncotype DX recurrence score <=18 -> class 0, >18 -> class 1 (optional 3-class <=18 / (18,31] / >31). These cut-offs are research definitions of this project, not clinical guidance. oncotype_score is never used as a predictor.
meta.placeholderNote: All examples in this viewer are illustrative placeholders (IDs such as PLACEHOLDER-P001). No real patient data is shown or was read to build it.

stages.name: Make synthetic data
stages.summary: Creates a small, completely made-up dataset that has the same file formats as the real Duke data. This lets you run and test the whole pipeline on a laptop without any patient data.
stages.purpose: Stand-in for the real Duke inputs in CPU acceptance runs and tests.

inputs.name: Command-line options
inputs.description: number of fake patients, random seed, volume size

outputs.name: Synthetic Duke-style workbooks
outputs.description: clinical features, NBIA metadata digest, imaging features, annotation boxes (.xlsx)

outputs.name: nifti/<SeriesInstanceUID>.nii.gz
outputs.description: fake 3D MRI phases with a bright ellipsoid 'lesion'

details: Alternative to stages 'Download DICOM' + 'DICOM -> NIfTI': point experiment.conf PATHS (or configs/synthetic_cpu_*.conf) at runs/synthetic/data.
Used by the CPU acceptance configs configs/synthetic_cpu_2d.conf and synthetic_cpu_3d*.conf and by tests/e2e.

stages.name: Download DICOM (NBIA/TCIA)
stages.summary: Downloads the raw MRI scans (DICOM files) of the Duke Breast Cancer MRI collection from the public TCIA/NBIA archive, only for patients that have an Oncotype score.
stages.purpose: Fetch raw DICOM series for the outcome cohort.

inputs.name: NBIA metadata digest (.xlsx/.csv)
inputs.description: lists Patient ID, Study/Series Instance UIDs

inputs.name: Clinical workbook
inputs.description: needed for --cohort outcome (patients with an Oncotype score)

outputs.name: <dest>/<SeriesInstanceUID>/
outputs.description: DICOM files per series, plus a download manifest

details: Separate stage with its own optional dependencies (pip install -e .[prepare]); train/validate never import prepare/.
Zip members are checked for unsafe paths before extraction (_safe_members).
uncertain: Only exercised against local fakes; real TCIA downloads have not been run (docs/acceptance.md §5).

stages.name: DICOM -> NIfTI
stages.summary: Converts each downloaded scan from many DICOM slice files into one 3D NIfTI file, after checking that the scan ID and the slice geometry are consistent.
stages.purpose: Produce <image_root>/<SeriesInstanceUID>.nii.gz, the image format the pipeline reads.
details: Raises SeriesUidMismatch / GeometryError instead of writing a doubtful volume.
Matches the legacy SimpleITK path on synthetic oblique series: voxels exact, affine within 1e-4 mm (docs/acceptance.md).
uncertain: Tested on synthetic series only; enhanced / multi-frame MR (if present in Duke) has not been tried.

stages.name: Lesion masks (MRI-CORE/SAM)
stages.summary: Uses a pretrained segmentation model (MRI-CORE, based on SAM) to draw a lesion outline inside each radiologist's bounding box. The result is a mask file per study that the image model can later use to focus on the tumour.
stages.purpose: Box-prompted lesion segmentation -> mask manifest for mask_provider=local_files.

inputs.name: Cohort
inputs.description: built from clinical + metadata tables (same DukeCohortSource as training), or --cohort_csv

outputs.name: masks/<study_id>.nii.gz
outputs.description: uint8 {0 background, 1 lesion} on the first series' grid

details: Per slice: square context window around the box, percentile clipping [0.5, 99.5], min-max to uint8, 3 channels, resize to 1024^2, ImageNet normalisation, box prompt, 3 masks, choose best IoU, threshold logits, paste back, clip to box +- margin.
Resumable: a study is skipped when its sidecar settings_fingerprint matches; files published with os.replace; manifest and COMPLETE written last.
Never use the repo's num_cls=1 setup zero-shot (random mask tokens); the project's own loader reproduces the num_cls=3 build.
Masks only exist where a Duke box exists, so a classifier using them needs the box at inference (requires_box_at_inference=true).
uncertain: Not verified on any real Duke slice: mask quality and the box axis convention of the prompts are unchecked (docs/acceptance.md §4b).
Zero-shot quality measured on toy 2D images only; MRI-CORE pretraining overlap with Duke unknown.

stages.name: MRI-CORE embeddings
stages.summary: Runs a frozen, pretrained MRI foundation model (MRI-CORE) over the slices inside each radiologist's lesion box and turns them into a list of numbers (an embedding) per study. These numbers can then be used by the tabular model as an extra feature group, next to the clinical data.
stages.purpose: Frozen-encoder study embeddings -> CSV for feature group mricore (PATHS[mricore_features_file]).

inputs.name: Cohort
inputs.description: built from clinical + metadata tables (same DukeCohortSource as training, --profile)

inputs.name: Annotation_Boxes.xlsx
inputs.description: Duke lesion boxes; needed for --pool roi / both

inputs.name: NIfTI volumes
inputs.description: image_root (read only; the output may not be inside it)

outputs.name: <output>.csv
outputs.description: patient_id, study_id, series_uid, phase, n_slices + mricore_<pool>_<k> (768 per pool)

outputs.name: <stem>_audit.csv
outputs.description: one row per cohort study with status / detail

outputs.name: <stem>_provenance.json
outputs.description: checkpoint sha256, MRI-CORE git commit, arguments, weight-loading check, counts

parameters.note: index into the study's ordered series (0 = pre, 1 = first post-contrast)
box slices evenly thinned to this many
box widening per side for roi pooling

details: Per volume: clip to [0.5, 99.5] percentiles, scale to [0, 1]; per slice: resize to --image_size, 3 channels, ImageNet normalisation (MRI-CORE normalize_type=ours).
Frozen ViT-B image encoder, no adapters, weights loaded strictly; 768-d patch tokens average-pooled over the box (roi) and/or the whole slice (global), then averaged over slices.
Label-free and applied to each study independently, so the features carry no fold information and are computed once for the whole cohort.
Studies without a row (no NIfTI, or no box with --pool roi) get NaN and are imputed fold-locally like any predictor; predictor policy allows the mricore_ prefix.
uncertain: Not yet run on real Duke data; the embeddings' predictive value for the Oncotype label is unknown.
MRI-CORE pretraining overlap with Duke unknown.

stages.name: Experiment controller
stages.summary: Reads the experiment settings file, expands the grid of settings to try (for example 3 network types x 2 feature sets x 2 tabular models x 2 loss weights = 24 runs), and launches one job per combination, either on the Slurm cluster or one after another on this computer.
stages.purpose: Turn experiment.conf + fields.tsv into one exact Python command line per grid row, frozen in a snapshot.

inputs.name: experiment.conf / configs/*.conf
inputs.description: PATHS, TRAIN, TRAIN_GRID, VALIDATE, VALIDATE_GRID, SUMMARIZE, JOB_* resources

inputs.name: Prepared input files
inputs.description: workbooks, NIfTI directory, optional mask manifest (referenced in PATHS)

outputs.name: argv per task
outputs.description: python -m mribreast <stage> --key value ... (identical for Slurm and --local)

outputs.name: <slurm_logs>/run-<stage>-<timestamp>/
outputs.description: read-only snapshot: resolved config, controller copy, fields.tsv, code_version.txt

parameters.note: run tasks here instead of sbatch
mri_model x feature_groups x feature_model x sensitivity_lambda

details: Grid keys are sorted; the last sorted key varies fastest (legacy select_grid). Verified identical to the reference controller for all 24 rows.
Validation task i = training row i / |VALIDATE_GRID|, validation row i % |VALIDATE_GRID| (24 tasks for one alpha, 72 for three).
The controller never computes train_id / eval_id; Python is authoritative.
Stages are chained with --dependency afterok:<id> on Slurm (train -> validate -> summarize).
stages.loop: One task per grid row (train, validate) or one task (summarize).
stages.example: PLACEHOLDER task: python -m mribreast train --mri_model resnet10 --feature_model xgboost --sensitivity_lambda 0.05 ...
uncertain: Helios GH200 runtime (sbatch, module load ML-bundle, real flock, ARM venv bootstrap) has not been exercised (docs/acceptance.md §5).

stages.name: Resolve config & IDs
stages.summary: Checks every setting against the registry, rejects combinations that do not make sense, confirms the input files exist, and computes short IDs (train_id, eval_id) that uniquely name this exact experiment, so results are never mixed up.
stages.purpose: Typed, validated configuration plus deterministic identities for artifacts.

inputs.name: Input files
inputs.description: content fingerprints of identity paths that this mode needs

parameters.note: parallelism, output/cache roots and experiment_id are excluded from identity
enter the identity only when box_mode != none (keeps old train_ids stable)

details: Runs at the start of every Python stage: prepare, train and validate each resolve the config, build the cohort and recompute train_id independently.

Lesion location comes from exactly one source: external masks (mask_mode), Duke boxes as model input (box_mode, 3D only), or mask-based 2D slice selection. Combinations are rejected in validate_combinations.
required_inputs lists which path keys this mode actually needs (e.g. annotation_boxes_file only with boxes).

stages.name: Prepare: audit & cache warm-up
stages.summary: An optional dry run before training: it builds the patient list, writes reports of who was included or excluded and why, and pre-computes the resized images so training does not have to.
stages.purpose: Cohort audit + deterministic image-cache warm-up, no training.

outputs.name: <checkpoint_root>/_prepare/<train_id>/
outputs.description: cohort.csv (no oncotype_score), cohort_audit.csv, mask/box audits, prepare_manifest.json

outputs.name: Warm cache
outputs.description: prepared_root / subtraction_root entries reused by training

details: Cache key = sha256 of {cache schema, source UIDs + file fingerprints, target_size, normalisation, resize backend}; writers take an exclusive lock and publish with os.replace.
Augmentations are never cached.

stages.name: Build cohort & labels
stages.summary: Reads the clinical spreadsheet and the scan list, keeps patients that have an Oncotype score, turns the score into a label (low risk 0 / high risk 1), and picks which MRI series (contrast phases) belong to each study.
stages.purpose: One row per study: patient_id, study_id, label, ordered series_uids (+ audit of every exclusion).

inputs.name: NBIA metadata digest
inputs.description: sheet 'Metadata': Patient ID, Study/Series Instance UID, Series Description

parameters.note: shipped Duke configs and campaign: general

details: duke_legacy_3d: series = the first phase_count series of each study in metadata row order (bit-compatible with the legacy repo). On the real Duke digest this puts the non-DCE 'ax t1' series into 220/261 studies in arbitrary order; use it only to reproduce legacy numbers.

general: phases parsed from series descriptions; an unlabelled pre-contrast series named like its posts without the phase token ('ax 3d dyn' next to 'Ph1/ax 3d dyn') becomes phase 0. Requires pre-contrast + consecutive post-contrast phases, otherwise the study is excluded with a reason.
Real Duke data (checked 2026-11-25): general / explicit / phase_count=4 keeps 257 of 261 scored studies (159 / 98), one geometry across phases, every annotation box inside the volume.
Final inner join with the clinical table; oncotype_score is dropped before anything is written.
stages.example: PLACEHOLDER row: patient_id=PLACEHOLDER-P001, study_id=PLACEHOLDER-S001, label=1, series_uids=UID-A|UID-B|UID-C|UID-D|UID-E
uncertain: The NBIA digest is not in either repository; its column names were inferred from legacy code (they load correctly on the real digest).
No training or evaluation has been run on real Duke data.

stages.name: Attach tabular features
stages.summary: Adds the non-image information for each study: clinical facts (e.g. age, tumour characteristics) and, optionally, numeric features already computed from the images. A safety check makes sure nothing that reveals the answer is used as an input.
stages.purpose: Join the configured feature groups and enforce the allowed-predictor policy.
details: Policy check is name-based (primary control) plus a data-based leakage check.
Density with <50% coverage adds a warning; missing values are imputed fold-locally later.
uncertain: The data-based label-leak check catches only exact copies of the score (documented limitation, docs/acceptance.md §4).

stages.name: Patient-grouped split plan
stages.summary: Divides patients into 5 groups (folds). Each fold in turn is held out for testing while the model learns on the others; the learning part is split again to keep some patients aside for choosing the best model and the decision cut-off. All scans of one patient always stay in the same group, so the model is never tested on someone it has seen.
stages.purpose: Frozen nested-CV plan with roles fit / calibration (or selection + threshold) / outer_eval, and the train manifest.

inputs.name: Cohort frame
inputs.description: labels + patient_id groups, in cohort order

outputs.name: split_manifest.csv
outputs.description: fold, patient_id, study_id, label, role, inner-fold metadata; its sha256 = split_hash

outputs.name: train_manifest.json
outputs.description: ids, resolved config, input + cohort fingerprints, split_hash, versions

parameters.note: first inner fold is held out as calibration
outer seed; inner seed = seed + fold

details: shared (legacy fusion): calibration patients pick the checkpoint AND tune thresholds.
separate: calibration patients are split again (seed + fold + 1000) into selection and threshold.
outer (historical image-only): the outer fold selects the checkpoint and is evaluated - optimistic, flagged as selection_uses_outer_eval.
Frozen: an existing split_manifest.csv is reused and verified, never regenerated. An existing train dir with different identity raises ArtifactMismatch.
Leakage checks live in tests/review/test_review_splits_leakage.py.
stages.example: PLACEHOLDER: fold 1 -> fit: 60% of patients, calibration: 20%, outer_eval: 20%

stages.name: Image loading & preprocessing
stages.summary: Loads the MRI phases of each study, normalises their brightness, resizes them to a fixed size and stacks them as channels. Depending on the settings it can also crop to the tumour, add a mask channel, or cut 2D slices. During training it randomly blanks a patch of background as data augmentation.
stages.purpose: Turn studies into model-ready tensors [C, D, H, W] (3D) or [C, H, W] (2D items).

inputs.name: fit + selection rows of this fold

outputs.name: ItemTable + ImageDataset
outputs.description: (x, y, study_index) items; dual_stream yields (global, local)

details: subtraction_mode=none: load -> z-score whole volume (population std, no epsilon) -> trilinear resize (align_corners=False). Normalisation before resize, as in legacy MONAI.
Subtraction: verify same grid -> resize raw phases -> minuend - subtrahend -> z-score with +1e-5. Channels: phase_count (5) or phase_count - 1 (4); +1 for mask_channel.
Crops (mask roi_crop, box roi_crop/dual_stream) are computed on the NATIVE grid before resizing, so small lesions are not lost.
Erasing: one background cuboid of side dim//4, up to 8 draws, rejected if it touches the lesion box; fit rows only; RNG = default_rng([seed, epoch, item]).
Mask policies (missing/empty/invalid): error | full_image | drop; every decision is audited.
stages.example: PLACEHOLDER tensor: 4 channels x 256 x 256 x 64 (pre + 3 post-contrast phases, shipped Duke configs)
uncertain: Annotation-box convention (0-based inclusive, column/row/slice -> array axes 0/1/2) is reproduced from legacy code only and has not been checked against real DICOM overlays. Treat box-based results as provisional (docs/imaging.md §4).

stages.name: Train image model
stages.summary: Trains a 3D convolutional neural network (DenseNet or ResNet) to predict the risk label from the images. After each pass over the training patients it checks performance on the held-aside patients and keeps the best version.
stages.purpose: Fit the image branch on fit rows; pick the checkpoint by ROC-AUC on selection rows.

outputs.name: image_branch.json
outputs.description: network, imaging, mask/box settings, class weights, best epoch, counts

details: Class weights: total / (K * max(count, 1)), positive class multiplied by positive_boost.
ModelCheckpoint(monitor=val_auc_roc, mode=max, save_top_k=1, save_last=True). Metrics are computed per study.
Training loader is not shuffled (legacy); a trailing batch of exactly one sample is dropped (BatchNorm).
Probabilities use a float64 softmax to avoid artificial ROC-AUC ties.
stages.example: PLACEHOLDER: best epoch 12 of 30, val_auc_roc = PLACEHOLDER

stages.name: Train tabular model
stages.summary: Trains a classic machine-learning model (gradient-boosted trees or a small neural network) on the spreadsheet features. Missing values are filled in and, optionally, a LASSO step keeps only the most useful features.
stages.purpose: Fit preprocessor -> optional LASSO selector -> XGBoost or MLP on fit rows.

outputs.name: fold_<k>/tabular/
outputs.description: preprocessor.joblib, selector.joblib, model.joblib, feature_names.txt, selected_feature_names.txt, coefficients.csv, lasso_feature_selection.csv, tabular_branch.json, *.png

libraries: scikit-learn (SimpleImputer, StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder, LogisticRegressionCV l1/saga, MLPClassifier)
details: Continuous: median imputation + standardisation. Categorical: most-frequent imputation + one-hot (unknown categories ignored).
LASSO CV folds are grouped by patient; a minimum-feature fallback keeps at least lasso_min_features.
Selection rows are NOT used by the tabular branch (selection_rows_used=false).
duke_legacy_3d profile: every fold uses the global seed for XGBoost/MLP/LASSO (legacy behaviour).
stages.example: PLACEHOLDER: LASSO kept 7 of 42 features in fold 1

stages.name: Publish fold (resumable)
stages.summary: Saves everything learned in this fold in one go and marks it COMPLETE. If the job crashes, a restart skips finished folds and redoes only the unfinished one. After the last fold the whole training run is marked complete.
stages.purpose: Atomic, verifiable fold artifacts; loop to the next outer fold; finalise the training run.

outputs.name: fold_<k>/fold_manifest.json + COMPLETE
outputs.description: role counts, inner-fold metadata, sha256 of every branch artifact

details: Resume: a fold is skipped only if fold_k/COMPLETE exists and fold_manifest.json matches the current train_id and split_hash.
predictor.save must be idempotent and use relative paths because the staging directory is renamed on publish.
stages.loop: Repeats image preprocessing -> image fit -> tabular fit -> publish for each outer fold (default 5).

stages.name: Verify training artifacts
stages.command: bash run_experiment.sh --validate  ->  python -m mribreast validate ... -> run_validation
stages.summary: Before scoring anything, validation recomputes the experiment ID and checks that the saved training run really belongs to this exact configuration, data and split. If anything differs it stops with an error instead of producing misleading numbers.
stages.purpose: Reject mismatched or incomplete training runs; load predictors per fold.

inputs.name: Recomputed cfg, cohort, fingerprints
inputs.description: validate re-runs config resolution and cohort building

details: ArtifactMismatch when train_id, label definition, input fingerprints, cohort fingerprint or split hash differ.
Branch load() refuses artifacts trained with different geometry, channels, mask/box settings or class count.
An evaluation already marked COMPLETE with the same ids is returned unchanged.

stages.name: Predict each branch
stages.summary: Each trained model gives a probability of high risk for two groups of patients: the held-aside patients used to choose the cut-off, and the held-out test patients of this fold. Studies that one model could not score are removed from all models so the comparison is fair.
stages.purpose: Per-branch class probabilities on threshold-role rows and outer_eval rows, same denominator for all branches.

outputs.name: p_image, p_tabular
outputs.description: [n, C] probability arrays aligned by study_id

outputs.name: Excluded studies
outputs.description: studies with NaN rows (e.g. mask policy drop)

parameters.note: patient = average study probabilities per patient

details: A study excluded by ANY branch is excluded from ALL branches and fusion; counts go to excluded_studies.csv.
Partially missing probability rows raise an error.

stages.name: Late fusion
stages.summary: Combines the two opinions into one with a weighted average: alpha times the image model's probability plus (1 - alpha) times the tabular model's probability. Trying a different alpha does not require retraining.
stages.purpose: p_fusion = alpha * p_image + (1 - alpha) * p_tabular, row-renormalised.

outputs.name: p_fusion
outputs.description: added as a third branch when both image and tabular exist

parameters.note: image weight; part of eval_id only

details: alpha = 1 or 0 returns the single branch unchanged (avoids float noise changing ROC-AUC ties).
Alignment rejects missing, duplicate or unexpected studies and rows that are not distributions.
Skipped when only one branch is configured (branches=image or branches=tabular).

stages.name: Tune decision thresholds
stages.summary: Chooses, for each model separately, the probability cut-off above which a patient is called 'high risk'. It picks the cut-off with the best balanced accuracy on the held-aside patients, never on the test patients (except in the documented 'outer' mode).
stages.purpose: One threshold per branch (image, tabular, fusion) per fold; decisions p[:, pos] >= t.

outputs.name: Decisions
outputs.description: 0/1 per study on calibration and outer_eval rows

details: Candidates = unique({0, 0.5, 1} U scores); key = (balanced accuracy, sensitivity, -|t - 0.5|). Ported verbatim from legacy, locked by 400 tie-heavy test cases.
3-class label scheme: no threshold, argmax.

stages.name: Metrics & evaluation report
stages.summary: Measures how well each model did on the test patients of every fold (accuracy, balanced accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, ROC-AUC), pools all folds together, draws ROC curves and confusion matrices, and writes a readable report.
stages.purpose: Per-fold and pooled metrics; publish <validation_root>/<train_id>/<eval_id>/ with COMPLETE.
details: Pooled confusion matrix concatenates per-fold decisions, each made with that fold's own threshold; pooled ROC-AUC uses concatenated probabilities.
evaluation_manifest.json records selection_uses_outer_eval / threshold_uses_outer_eval.
stages.loop: Fold metrics are gathered in the fold loop; pooled outputs are written once after the last fold.

stages.name: Summarize & rank
stages.command: bash run_experiment.sh --summarize  ->  python -m mribreast summarize ... -> reporting.summarize.summarize
stages.summary: Collects the results of every experiment, averages them over folds, and ranks the configurations by ROC-AUC, then balanced accuracy, sensitivity and specificity of the main (usually fused) model. It points out the best one but warns that choosing it this way is itself a form of selection.
stages.purpose: Aggregate all evaluations, rank configurations, write the summary directory.
details: is_complete = folds 1..num_folds present AND a COMPLETE flag; incomplete runs are listed and warned about but not ranked by default.
Ranking columns primary_{auc_roc, balanced_accuracy, sensitivity, specificity}_mean; equal to the legacy fusion_* keys for fusion runs.
uncertain: Ranking reuses the outer folds, so the best configuration's scores are optimistic; a generalisation claim needs an independent test set or an extra nesting level (stated in every validation_report.md).

branchesAndOptions.title: Input source
branchesAndOptions.text: Real Duke data (download -> convert, optional MRI-CORE masks and/or MRI-CORE embeddings for the tabular branch) OR make-synthetic. Both end up as file paths in experiment.conf PATHS.

branchesAndOptions.title: Branches
branchesAndOptions.text: branches = image,tabular (default; fusion added automatically), image only, or tabular only. Fusion exists only when both branches are trained.

branchesAndOptions.title: Image mode
branchesAndOptions.text: 3D NIfTI (default), 2D slices cut from NIfTI, or ready 2D images (manifest_2d). Subtraction modes none | post_minus_pre | consecutive.

branchesAndOptions.title: Lesion location (exactly one)
branchesAndOptions.text: external masks (mask_mode roi_crop | mask_channel | foreground_only), Duke boxes as model input (box_mode roi_crop | box_channel | dual_stream, 3D only), or mask-based 2D slice selection. use_annotation_boxes is a separate augmentation (background erasing).

branchesAndOptions.title: Selection split
branchesAndOptions.text: shared (calibration picks checkpoint and threshold), separate (selection vs threshold patients), outer (historical, optimistic: uses outer_eval).

branchesAndOptions.title: Loops
branchesAndOptions.text: Grid rows (controller) x outer folds (train and validate). Validation additionally loops over VALIDATE_GRID (e.g. several fusion_alpha) without retraining.

branchesAndOptions.title: Resume
branchesAndOptions.text: Training skips folds with a matching COMPLETE flag; validation returns an existing COMPLETE evaluation; segmentation skips studies with a matching settings fingerprint.

sideTools.name: import-legacy
sideTools.text: Normalises historical mri_brest results (run ids lg-<hash>/ev-a<alpha>-legacy) into a separate output_dir. Not part of the main flow.

sideTools.name: mama-mia-download / mama-mia-map
sideTools.text: Maps MAMA-MIA series UIDs onto Duke series/patients. Its masks are not yet imported into the pipeline.

sideTools.name: nifti-info
sideTools.text: Lists the geometry of converted NIfTI files.

uncertainties.text: Cohort built and audited on real Duke data, but no model has been trained on it yet.
All 257 boxes fall inside their volumes, but the row/column axis order has not been checked against real overlays (square slices fit either way).
MRI-CORE masks not verified on real Duke slices.
MRI-CORE embeddings not yet computed on real Duke data.
TCIA download exercised only against fakes.
Ranking on the outer folds is optimistic for the selected configuration.
Data-based label-leak check detects exact copies only.
